_comment: Licence audit of the VideoLAN.LibVLC.Windows payload, checked by DiffusionNexus.Tests/Licensing/VlcPayloadLicenseTests.cs. VideoLAN.LibVLC.Windows declares LGPL-2.1-or-later, which is true of libvlc and libvlccore but NOT of everything the package carries. The test re-derives the GPL set from the shipped files on every run and fails if a file carrying GPL evidence is not classified here, so a VLC version bump cannot introduce one silently. Paths are relative to build/<rid>/ in the package and use forward slashes.
upstreamVersionSource: Read from libvlc.dll's version resource (FileVersion 3.0.23) and libvlccore.dll's embedded version string, NOT inferred from the NuGet package number 3.0.23.1, which differs.

shippedGpl.evidence: The binary states its own licence: 'libavcodec license: GPL version 2 or later'. Built with --enable-gpl --enable-postproc --enable-static --disable-shared.
shippedGpl.whyShipped: Required. Removing it was measured against real media and breaks HEVC and MPEG-4/AVI playback: the remaining decoders fall back to Windows Media Foundation, which does not cover those formats here.

staticallyLinked.evidence: Build flag --enable-libmp3lame present, plus LAME's own version stamp 'LAME3.100', its project URL 'http://lame.sf.net' and its runtime error strings. --enable-static --disable-shared means it is compiled into this plugin, not loaded from a separate DLL.
Build flag --enable-libopenjpeg present, plus 'OpenJPEG' strings in the binary.
Build flag --enable-libgsm present, plus 'libgsm' strings in the binary.

shippedGpl.evidence: The binary states its own licence: 'libswscale license: GPL version 2 or later'. Same FFmpeg build as libavcodec_plugin.dll.
shippedGpl.whyShipped: Required alongside libavcodec for the same playback paths.

excludedGpl.evidence: Module declares 'Licensed under the terms of the GNU General Public License, version 2 or later.'
excludedGpl.whyExcluded: An H.264 encoder. This application only plays video back; it never encodes through VLC.

excludedGpl.evidence: Module declares 'Licensed under the terms of the GNU General Public License, version 2 or later.'
excludedGpl.whyExcluded: VLC's Lua bindings, used for web-service playlist parsing and art fetching. Not reachable from local file playback. Excluding it is what makes the lua/** data tree dead weight, so that is excluded too.

excludedGpl.evidence: Module declares 'Licensed under the terms of the GNU General Public License, version 2 or later.'
excludedGpl.whyExcluded: An opt-in audio filter, only active if a user enables it. The video player exposes no such control.

excludedGpl.evidence: Module declares 'Licensed under the terms of the GNU General Public License, version 2 or later.'
excludedGpl.whyExcluded: An opt-in audio filter, as above.

excludedGpl.evidence: 16 of the 95 files carry a full GPL-2.0-or-later header ('This program is free software; you can redistribute it and/or modify it under the terms of the GNU General Public License as published by the Free Software Foundation; either version 2 of the License, or (at your option) any later version'): lua/http/{index,mobile,mobile_browse,mobile_equalizer,mobile_view,view,vlm}.html and lua/http/requests/{browse,playlist,status}.{json,xml}, playlist_jstree.xml, vlm.xml, vlm_cmd.xml.
excludedGpl.whyExcluded: 1.1 MB of web-interface assets for VLC's HTTP control server. liblua_plugin.dll is excluded, so nothing can ever load them. Shipping unattributed GPL dead weight for no function.

notLicenceDeclarations.matched: You may redistribute it under the terms of the GNU General Public License;
notLicenceDeclarations.matchedNote: Recorded without the following sentence because the string carries an embedded newline at that point.
notLicenceDeclarations.reason: VLC's command-line front-end banner, carried as a data string inside libvlccore - it describes the VLC *application*, which is GPL, not this library. libvlccore itself is LGPL-2.1-or-later: VideoLAN relicensed the core in 2012 precisely so libvlc could be embedded in non-GPL applications, and the package's own metadata agrees. Recorded here rather than silently filtered, because a detector tuned to avoid this one string would also miss a real declaration phrased differently.
